experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the most spectacular highlights including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. The trail winds through dramatic landscapes of granite peaks, turquoise lakes, and ancient forests, offering an unparalleled Patagonian wilderness experience.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the iconic base of the Torres del Paine towers to witness a breathtaking sunrise over the three granite monoliths reflected in the glacial lake below. This challenging 8-hour round trip hike rewards trekkers with one of the most photographed and awe-inspiring natural spectacles in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey alongside massive floating icebergs calved from the Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most impressive ice fields. This guided kayaking adventure along the lakeshore offers a unique water-level perspective of the glacier face and surrounding mountain scenery, combining water activity with raw natural beauty near the lake's edge.
experiences.location: Lago Grey Shoreline, Grey Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the stunning French Valley, a glacial amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering peaks including Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. The trail offers dramatic views of avalanches tumbling down steep cliffs and passes through native lenga beech forests alive with Andean condors soaring overhead.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Lago Pehoé Lakeside Nature Walk & Wildlife Spotting
experiences.description: Explore the serene shores of Lago Pehoé on a guided nature walk, spotting native Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and flamingos against the backdrop of the iconic Cuernos del Paine peaks. This moderate lakeside trail offers stunning reflections of the mountains on the turquoise waters and is ideal for nature photography and birdwatching.
experiences.location: Lago Pehoé Shoreline, Western Sector, Torres del Paine

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and arrange shared shuttle transfer to Puerto Natales (budget option ~$15-20 USD). Check in to overnight budget hostel in Puerto Natales and pick up park supplies at local supermarket (Unimarc or Erratic Rock). Stock up on trail snacks, instant noodles, and packed lunch items to save money inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free 'Patagonia Trek Talk' at Erratic Rock hostel in Puerto Natales (held nightly at 15:00 and again informally in the evening) — an invaluable free resource for trekkers. Walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront (Costanera) to watch the sunset over Última Esperanza Sound. Early dinner and rest to prepare for early park entry tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or skip — focus on arrival
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snack from convenience store (~$5 USD)
meals.dinner: Aldea Restaurant or Afrigonia in Puerto Natales — set menu 'menú del día' for ~$8-10 USD, or self-cook at hostel kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Book your park entrance permit in advance online at reservas.conaf.cl — it is mandatory and costs ~$35 USD per person. Also pre-book all campsites along the W or O Circuit as they fill up months in advance. Buy a local SIM card at the airport for offline maps (Maps.me or Gaia GPS recommended). Keep all receipts for budget tracking.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 06:00. Eat a hearty hostel breakfast or self-prepare oats and coffee. Board the 07:30 shared bus from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park entrance (Laguna Amarga sector) — cost ~$12-15 USD one way with Buses JB or Turismo Zaahj. Arrive at park entrance around 10:00, pay/show park entrance permit at CONAF gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer by free park catamaran shuttle or local bus from Laguna Amarga to the Towers trailhead area. Begin the iconic hike to Mirador Las Torres (Base de las Torres). The trail is 18 km round trip with 800m elevation gain — allow 7-8 hours total. Start the ascent through lenga beech forest and rocky moraine. Reach the stunning glacial teal lake at the base of the granite Torres del Paine towers — one of Patagonia's most spectacular viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to Camping Torres (Campamento Torres) or Refugio Las Torres area. Set up tent at the campsite (~$10-12 USD per person at basic campsite). Cook a hot meal on camp stove using pre-bought supplies. Enjoy the long Patagonian summer daylight (sunset around 22:00). Stargaze if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Oats, instant coffee, and fruit prepared at hostel kitchen (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: sandwiches, energy bars, nuts, dried fruit (pre-bought in Puerto Natales ~$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal: pasta with tuna or instant noodles with vegetables (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear waterproof layers — Patagonian weather changes rapidly. Wind can be extreme, especially in the afternoon. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the rocky moraine ascent to Las Torres. Start early to avoid afternoon winds and crowds at the viewpoint.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 06:30 at Campamento Torres. Pack up camp and eat a warm breakfast. Begin trekking north along the Valley del Francés approach — hike through open Patagonian steppe toward Campamento Seron (~11 km, 3-4 hours). Enjoy expansive views of the Paine Massif and spot guanacos grazing on the plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking or rest at Campamento Seron. If energy allows, do a short exploratory walk along the Río Paine riverbank spotting Andean condors, flamingos, and black-necked swans. Set up tent at Campamento Seron (free CONAF campsite — book in advance). Afternoon is ideal for boot drying, gear maintenance, and journaling.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a warm camp dinner as temperatures drop. Share stories with fellow trekkers at the campsite. Enjoy the golden evening light over the Paine Massif. Early bedtime to prepare for a long trekking day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Instant oatmeal with powdered milk and raisins, instant coffee (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Trail mix, crackers with peanut butter, energy gels (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Freeze-dried meal or lentil soup with bread (~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Campamento Seron is a free CONAF-managed site but must be pre-booked. Water is available from the river — use a filter or purification tablets. This section of the O Circuit is less crowded than the W Trek, offering more solitude and wildlife encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 07:00. Trek from Campamento Seron toward Campamento Dickson (~18 km, 5-6 hours). The trail follows the Río Paine valley through stunning glacial landscapes. Cross open moorland with views of Lago Dickson and the Dickson Glacier — one of the most dramatic glacier views on the circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Campamento Dickson by early afternoon. Set up camp and rest tired legs. Take a short walk to the lakeside viewpoint for close-up views of Glaciar Dickson calving into the milky turquoise lake. Photograph guanacos and condors frequently spotted in this area.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner using camp stove supplies. This remote section of the O Circuit feels truly wild and isolated — embrace the silence and vast Patagonian wilderness. Watch the evening alpenglow turn the glacier pink and gold. Early rest.

meals.breakfast: Granola with powdered milk, hot tea (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: tuna wrap, nuts, chocolate bar (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Rice with dehydrated vegetables and olive oil, hot chocolate (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most remote section of the O Circuit. Weather can be severe — have full rain gear accessible. The trail between Seron and Dickson involves some river crossings on wooden bridges that may be slippery. No mobile signal in this area.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 06:30. Trek from Campamento Dickson to Campamento Los Perros (~9 km, 3-4 hours). This shorter day allows for a slower pace through spectacular scenery including lenga beech forest, hanging glaciers, and the wild Río de Los Perros valley. The trail gains significant elevation toward the end.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Campamento Los Perros by early afternoon. This is the base camp before the challenging John Gardner Pass. Use the afternoon to rest, hydrate, and prepare gear for tomorrow's big pass crossing. Explore the immediate surroundings — the valley is exceptionally beautiful and quiet.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and gear check for tomorrow's pass crossing. The John Gardner Pass (1,241m) is the highest point of the O Circuit and requires an early start. Lay out all gear, dry any wet clothing, and prepare tomorrow's packed lunch. Lights out by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and nuts, instant coffee (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Crackers, cheese (if still fresh), salami, dried mango (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pasta with tomato sauce and tuna, hot soup (~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Campamento Los Perros is a critical staging point for the John Gardner Pass crossing. Check weather carefully — the pass should NOT be attempted in high winds, whiteout conditions, or heavy snow. Rangers at the campsite will advise on conditions. Set alarm for 05:30 tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start at 06:00. The John Gardner Pass crossing to Campamento Paso (~22 km total to Grey campsite, 8-10 hours) is the most challenging and rewarding day of the O Circuit. Ascend steeply through forest and exposed rocky terrain to the 1,241m pass. At the summit, witness the breathtaking panoramic view of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field and Glaciar Grey — one of the most spectacular vistas in all of South America.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend steeply on the western side of the pass (can involve snow even in summer — microspikes helpful). Trek through ancient lenga beech forest draped in old man's beard lichen. Reach the shores of Lago Grey with its floating blue icebergs calved from Glaciar Grey. Continue to Campamento Paso or push to Refugio Grey depending on energy levels.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Campamento Paso or Grey area. Celebrate completing the hardest day of the trek with a special camp meal. Watch icebergs drift across Lago Grey in the evening light. This is a truly unforgettable wilderness experience.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast: oats with protein powder, nuts, coffee (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Energy-dense trail lunch eaten at the pass summit: bars, nuts, jerky (~$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory freeze-dried meal or hearty pasta, hot chocolate (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day — start early to avoid afternoon winds on the exposed pass. The descent is very steep and slippery when wet. Trekking poles are essential. In December the pass is usually snow-free but conditions vary. Always check with park rangers before attempting.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Grey campsite area. Sleep in until 07:30. After breakfast, take a leisurely walk along the shores of Lago Grey to observe icebergs up close. The pale blue ice chunks are hauntingly beautiful and come in extraordinary sculptural shapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in the featured experience: Lago Pehoé Lakeside Nature Walk & Wildlife Spotting. Trek or transfer toward the Lago Pehoé sector. Explore the serene lakeside trails spotting native Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, black-necked swans, flamingos, and possibly pumas (rare but present). The lake's turquoise waters reflect the Paine Massif dramatically.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Camping Pehoe or nearby budget campsite. Cook dinner and enjoy the magnificent sunset view of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in Lago Pehoé — arguably the most photographed scene in all of Patagonia. Journal, photograph, and rest.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely oatmeal, instant coffee, biscuits (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch by the lakeshore: crackers, peanut butter, fruit (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked rice and beans with spices, herbal tea (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to allow physical recovery after the John Gardner Pass crossing. The Lago Pehoé area is one of the most scenic in the park — take time to simply sit and absorb the landscape. Wildlife is most active in early morning and evening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike to Mirador Cuernos — a stunning viewpoint looking directly at the iconic Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine). The trail from Lago Pehoé area is approximately 4 km one way with moderate elevation gain. The granite and dark sedimentary rock contrast of the Cuernos is extraordinary in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek the Valle del Francés (French Valley) — one of the most dramatic hikes in the park. The valley is flanked by hanging glaciers, towering granite walls, and avalanche fields. Hike to Mirador Británico (the highest viewpoint in the valley) for 360-degree views of the Paine Massif, Glacier Francés, and surrounding peaks. Allow 5-6 hours round trip from the valley entrance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Campamento Italiano or Campamento Británico for the night. Cook a warm dinner and reflect on the extraordinary scenery of the French Valley. This is widely considered the most spectacular day hike in Torres del Paine. Rest well.

meals.breakfast: Quick oats and coffee before early start (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten at Mirador Británico: energy bars, nuts, dried fruit (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pasta with olive oil, garlic powder, and tuna, hot soup (~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Valle del Francés can have significant rockfall — stay on marked trails and wear a helmet if you have one. Avalanches from hanging glaciers are audible and visible throughout the day — an incredible natural spectacle. Wind in the valley can be very strong in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Campamento Italiano/Británico toward Refugio Los Cuernos (~6 km, 2 hours). This beautiful lakeside trail hugs the shores of Lago Nordenskjöld with stunning views of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in the water. Spot black-necked swans and upland geese along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Refugio Chileno area (~8 km further). Take a side trail to Mirador Los Cuernos for additional dramatic viewpoints. Alternatively, rest at a lakeside spot and do some birdwatching — this section of the park is excellent for Andean condors soaring on thermals above the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Camping Chileno or Torres area. Prepare for the pre-dawn Las Torres summit hike tomorrow — this is the classic 'sunrise at the towers' experience. Prepare packed breakfast and lunch for tomorrow. Early bedtime at 20:30.

meals.breakfast: Granola bars and instant coffee — quick and easy (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic: crackers, cheese if available, nuts, chocolate (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Hearty lentil stew with bread, hot tea (~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Set alarm for 04:00 tomorrow for the pre-dawn Las Torres hike to catch sunrise at the towers. This is one of the most magical experiences in Patagonia — the towers glow red and orange at first light. Pack headlamps, warm layers, and extra snacks for the early morning ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake at 04:00. Hike by headlamp to Mirador Las Torres for SUNRISE — the granite towers turn vivid shades of red, orange, and gold as the first light hits them. This is one of the most iconic sunrise experiences in South America. The 9 km ascent takes approximately 3-4 hours — aim to arrive at the lake before 07:00. Spend time at the towers as the light changes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to the trailhead by midday. Rest, eat a proper meal, and begin the trek or transfer back toward the park exit at Laguna Amarga. Catch the afternoon bus from Laguna Amarga back to Puerto Natales (~14:00 or 16:00 departure). Arrive in Puerto Natales by late afternoon. Check in to budget hostel.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Puerto Natales! Celebrate completing the O Circuit (or W Trek) with a proper sit-down dinner at a local restaurant. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal as a reward for completing one of the world's great treks. Explore the festive Puerto Natales waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy bars and thermos of coffee consumed on the trail at sunrise (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Celebratory post-hike meal at Refugio Las Torres café or packed lunch (~$6 USD)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve dinner at Afrigonia or El Living restaurant in Puerto Natales — splurge slightly at ~$15-18 USD for a proper meal with local lamb or seafood

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a significant celebration in Chilean culture — restaurants may be busy, book ahead if possible. The sunrise at Las Torres is weather-dependent — cloudy mornings still produce a beautiful experience but clear skies are magical. This marks the completion of the main trekking circuit.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — rest and recovery in Puerto Natales. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Museo Histórico Municipal de Puerto Natales (free or minimal entry) to learn about the history of Patagonia, indigenous Kawésqar people, and early European settlers. Walk along the Costanera waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Puerto Natales town: visit the local artisan market for Patagonian souvenirs (wool products, local crafts). Browse the Erratic Rock gear shop and pick up any needed supplies. Optional: rent a bicycle (~$10 USD/day) and cycle to Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument (24 km round trip) — a massive cave where a prehistoric ground sloth was discovered. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner in Puerto Natales — many restaurants offer special Christmas menus. Enjoy a celebratory meal with fellow travelers met on the trail. Share stories from the O Circuit. Alternatively, self-cook a special meal at the hostel using local ingredients: fresh seafood, Patagonian lamb chops, or centolla (king crab) if budget allows.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or café: medialunas, coffee, fresh juice (~$4 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café or supermarket deli (~$6 USD)
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner — local restaurant set menu or self-cooked special meal (~$12-15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Many businesses in Puerto Natales may be closed or have reduced hours on Christmas Day. The Cueva del Milodón is worth visiting if open — confirm hours in advance. Use this day to do laundry, recharge electronics, reorganize gear, and update travel journals. Book any onward transport needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along the Puerto Natales Costanera waterfront — the views of Última Esperanza Sound with flamingos wading in the shallows are beautiful in the morning light. Pack all gear and check out of hostel. Store luggage if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration of Puerto Natales: visit any remaining local spots, buy last-minute souvenirs, and have a farewell lunch. Arrange shared shuttle transfer back to Punta Arenas airport (~3 hours, ~$15-20 USD) or continue to next destination. If time allows before transfer, visit the small artisan shops on Calle Baquedano for hand-knitted Patagonian wool goods at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Puerto Natales toward Punta Arenas or onward destination. Reflect on an extraordinary 12 days in one of the world's most remote and spectacular wilderness areas. The memories of the Torres del Paine granite towers, the Southern Ice Field, glacial lakes, and Patagonian wildlife will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final hostel breakfast or café: eggs, toast, coffee (~$4 USD)
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at La Mesita Grande (pizza) or Patagonia Dulce (café) in Puerto Natales (~$8-10 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport café in Punta Arenas or packed snacks for travel (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 12 days: Park entrance ~$35 USD, Transport ~$60-80 USD, Campsites ~$80-100 USD (12 nights average), Food ~$120-150 USD (mix of self-cooked and restaurant), Miscellaneous ~$30-50 USD. Grand total: approximately $325-415 USD for the 12 days excluding flights. Always carry cash (Chilean pesos) as card payment is unreliable in remote areas. Leave no trace — pack out all waste from the park.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, arrange ground transfer (shared shuttle or rental car) to Puerto Natales (~1.5 hrs). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Puerto Natales for the night to rest before entering the park tomorrow. Take a short stroll along the Última Esperanza Sound waterfront to stretch your legs and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the compact center of Puerto Natales. Visit a local gear shop to pick up any last-minute trekking supplies, snacks, or park maps. Relax with a pisco sour at a cozy bar.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a coffee and medialunas at the airport café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light sandwich or empanadas at a café in Puerto Natales upon arrival — try Café Almacén Patagonia for affordable homemade fare.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Living Restaurant in Puerto Natales — a beloved mid-range spot with hearty lamb stew, soups, and vegetarian options; approx. USD 15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Do not enter Torres del Paine National Park today — focus on rest, resupply, and logistics. Confirm your park entry reservation (CONAF requires advance online booking). Ensure trekking poles, rain gear, and layering clothes are ready. Stock up on trail snacks and water purification tablets.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast and depart Puerto Natales by 07:30 via shared shuttle or rental car to Torres del Paine National Park entrance (~1.5 hrs). Pay park entry fee (approx. USD 35 for foreigners) and receive your CONAF safety briefing. Arrive at the park and check into your Boutique Stay accommodation in the Central Circuit area. Drop off main luggage and pack a daypack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a gentle introductory walk along the shores of Lago Pehoé — a perfect orientation hike to acclimate to the Patagonian terrain, altitude, and unpredictable weather. Spot Andean condors, guanacos, and flamingos along the lakeside trail. The turquoise waters framed by the Paine Massif make for stunning first photographs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Attend an optional evening orientation talk hosted by park rangers or lodge naturalists about the W Trek route, Leave No Trace principles, and wildlife safety. Organize your gear for the multi-day trek beginning tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Included at your Puerto Natales guesthouse — typically bread, eggs, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from supplies purchased in Puerto Natales. Eat lakeside at Lago Pehoé with panoramic mountain views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique lodge's on-site restaurant — expect a set menu featuring Patagonian lamb, fresh vegetables, and local wine; approx. USD 25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: December is peak Patagonian summer — days are very long (light until 22:00+). Weather can shift rapidly from sun to wind and rain within hours; always carry a waterproof jacket. Confirm W Trek segment bookings and refugio reservations for Days 3–7.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Trek — Day 1 of the iconic multi-day route. Start at the Laguna Amarga entrance and hike toward Las Torres base camp. The morning trail winds through lenga beech forest and open Patagonian steppe with guanaco sightings almost guaranteed. Approx. 8 km of moderate hiking to reach Refugio Las Torres.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Refugio Las Torres up the steep rocky ascent (approx. 2.5 km, +400m elevation gain) to the Mirador Las Torres viewpoint. The iconic granite towers rise dramatically above a glacial teal lake. Spend time at the mirador soaking in the views — one of Patagonia's most iconic panoramas. Begin descent back to Refugio Las Torres by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Las Torres for check-in. Hot shower, dry clothes, and a well-earned rest. Socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world in the communal dining area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique lodge before departure — hearty oats, eggs, and coffee to fuel the day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the base of the Torres — sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit, and nuts.
meals.dinner: Hearty set dinner at Refugio Las Torres — typically includes soup, a main course (beef or vegetarian option), and dessert; approx. USD 30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Total hiking distance today: approx. 19–22 km round trip including the mirador ascent. This is the most physically demanding day of the W Trek. Start early to avoid afternoon wind gusts. Trekking poles strongly recommended for the rocky ascent. Carry at least 2L of water.

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Wake at 04:30 for the legendary Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — hike back up to the base of the towers before dawn to witness the first golden light illuminate the granite spires reflected in the glacial lake below. This is one of the most photographed moments in all of Patagonia. Return to Refugio Las Torres for breakfast by 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek westward from Las Torres toward Valle del Francés, passing through open valley terrain with views of Lago Nordenskjöld. This section covers approximately 11 km with moderate undulation. Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos by mid-afternoon. Rest, explore the lakeshore, and photograph the dramatic Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine) reflecting in the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Refugio Los Cuernos. Enjoy the communal atmosphere, compare trail notes with other trekkers, and review tomorrow's Valle del Francés route on your map.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Refugio Las Torres after the sunrise hike return — eggs, toast, and hot drinks.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the trail between Las Torres and Los Cuernos — energy-dense trail mix, crackers, and cheese.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — set menu with Patagonian-style lamb or pasta, salad, and warm soup; approx. USD 30–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise hike requires re-ascending ~400m in darkness — bring a reliable headlamp with fresh batteries. If weather is overcast, the sunrise may be obscured but the experience of the silent pre-dawn hike is still worthwhile. Total hiking today (including sunrise hike): approx. 16–19 km.

day_by_day.morning: Valle del Francés Trekking Day — depart Refugio Los Cuernos early and hike into the stunning French Valley (Valle del Francés), a glacial amphitheater considered the most dramatic section of the W Trek. Trek up through lenga beech forest as the valley opens to reveal hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering granite walls on all sides. Reach the lower mirador (Mirador Británico viewpoint) for sweeping 360-degree views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the upper Valle del Francés viewpoint if weather and energy permit — reward yourself with views of the Paine Grande glacier and the full cirque of peaks. Begin descent back through the valley. The afternoon light creates extraordinary photography conditions as shadows shift across the hanging glaciers. Return to Los Cuernos or continue to Refugio Paine Grande.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Paine Grande on the western shore of Lago Pehoé. This is the largest refugio on the W Trek and has excellent facilities. Rest your legs, hang wet gear to dry, and enjoy the sunset over Lago Pehoé with Paine Grande peak as the backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos — oatmeal, bread with jam, and coffee before the early start.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Valle del Francés upper viewpoint — an unforgettable lunch location surrounded by glaciers and granite.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — buffet-style set menu with soup, main, and dessert; approx. USD 32–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is the scenic highlight of the entire W Trek. Total distance today: approx. 20–24 km depending on how far into the valley you hike. Watch and listen for ice calving from the hanging glaciers — a thunderous natural spectacle. Wind can be extremely strong in the open valley sections.

day_by_day.morning: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — depart Refugio Paine Grande and take the short trail or catamaran transfer to Lago Grey. Join a guided Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition and paddle through the icy steel-blue waters of Lago Grey alongside massive floating icebergs calved from the Grey Glacier. Your guide will explain glacial geology, Patagonian ecology, and point out wildlife including black-necked swans and Andean condors overhead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the kayaking expedition approaching the face of the Grey Glacier — a towering wall of blue ice stretching 6 km wide. After the kayaking session, take the trail along Lago Grey's eastern shore back toward Refugio Grey for a warm lunch and rest. Optional short hike to the Grey Glacier viewpoint on the lakeshore trail for a different perspective of the ice field.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Paine Grande via the lakeshore trail (approx. 11 km) or by catamaran. Rest and celebrate completing the western arm of the W Trek. Enjoy a relaxed evening with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande before the kayaking departure — eggs, toast, and hot drinks.
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at Refugio Grey after the kayaking expedition — soup and a warm main course; approx. USD 18–25.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — hearty set menu to refuel after a full day of paddling and hiking; approx. USD 32–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition must be pre-booked — confirm your reservation before the trip. Dry bags are provided but bring a change of clothes in a dry bag of your own. Water temperature is near freezing — wetsuits and safety gear are provided. This is one of the most unique and memorable experiences in all of Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Complete the final section of the W Trek — hike from Refugio Paine Grande back eastward along the southern shore of Lago Pehoé and Lago Nordenskjöld. This section offers the classic postcard view of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in the lake. A moderate 11 km trail with excellent wildlife spotting opportunities — guanacos, foxes, and birds are commonly seen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Pudeto catamaran dock and take the scenic 30-minute catamaran crossing back across Lago Pehoé. Return to your Central Circuit Boutique Stay accommodation. Check in, shower, and rest. You have officially completed the W Trek — a major achievement.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at the boutique lodge. Reflect on the week's trekking highlights. Optional: soak in any available hot tub or sauna facilities at the lodge to recover tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande — final refugio breakfast before returning to the boutique lodge.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten on the Lago Nordenskjöld shoreline with stunning Cuernos views.
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at the boutique lodge restaurant — treat yourself to a full Patagonian lamb asado (barbecue) if available, paired with a Carménère or Malbec; approx. USD 35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Pudeto catamaran runs on a fixed schedule — check times in advance (typically 09:00, 12:00, and 18:00 in high season). Book your catamaran ticket at Refugio Paine Grande the evening before. Total W Trek distance completed over Days 3–7: approximately 70–80 km — a genuine achievement worth celebrating.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the boutique lodge, and let your legs recover. Spend time journaling, reviewing photographs, or reading on the lodge terrace with views of the Paine Massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lago Pehoé Lakeside Nature Walk & Wildlife Spotting — join a guided nature walk along the serene shores of Lago Pehoé. A local naturalist guide leads a 3–4 hour interpretive walk identifying native Patagonian flora (calafate berries, mata barrosa, lenga beech), fauna (guanacos, grey foxes, Andean condors, flamingos, and black-necked swans), and explaining the park's unique sub-polar ecosystem. A relaxed, low-intensity experience perfect for a recovery day.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session from the lakeshore — December sunsets in Patagonia occur after 22:00, offering extraordinary extended golden hour light. Return to the lodge for a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique lodge — enjoy the full spread without rushing.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge café or packed picnic taken on the nature walk — sandwiches, fruit, and local calafate berry juice.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — order à la carte for a change of pace; try centolla (king crab) if available, or a hearty Patagonian stew; approx. USD 25–35.

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional recovery day — your legs need rest after 5 consecutive days of trekking. The guided nature walk is low-intensity and highly educational. Ask your guide about the park's conservation history, the 2011–2012 wildfire recovery, and current rewilding programs.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Mirador Ferrier — an off-the-beaten-path viewpoint above Lago Pehoé offering one of the most panoramic views in the entire park. The trail climbs steeply through lenga beech forest before emerging onto open ridgeline with 360-degree views of the Paine Massif, Grey Glacier, Lago Pehoé, and the Patagonian steppe stretching to the horizon. Approx. 4–5 hours round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Mirador Ferrier and spend the afternoon exploring the area around the Salto Chico waterfall near the park administration center (CONAF). Visit the CONAF visitor center to learn about the park's natural history, geology, and ongoing conservation efforts. Browse the exhibits on Patagonian wildlife and the Torres del Paine biosphere reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique lodge. Optional: arrange a private stargazing session — Torres del Paine has exceptional dark skies in summer (though full darkness is limited due to long days). In late December, the Southern Cross, Magellanic Clouds, and Milky Way core are visible from approximately 01:00 onward.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the Ferrier hike departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Mirador Ferrier summit — arguably the best lunch view in Patagonia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the park administration area or at the lodge — try a mixed grill (parrillada) with local sausages and Patagonian lamb chops; approx. USD 25–35.

day_by_day.notes: Mirador Ferrier is less crowded than the main W Trek viewpoints — an excellent choice for solitude and photography. The trail is unmarked in sections; carry a detailed park map or download offline GPS. Wear sun protection — the ridgeline is fully exposed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a guided excursion to the northern sector of the park — visit Laguna Azul and Laguna Amarga, two stunning lakes in the less-visited eastern zone of Torres del Paine. These lagoons sit on the Patagonian steppe and offer exceptional flamingo and rhea (ñandú) spotting. The landscape here is dramatically different from the western glacial zone — open, windswept, and vast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laguna Azul mirador for reflections of the Torres del Paine towers in the calm lake waters. Explore the eastern steppe trails on foot — look for pumas (rarely seen but present), guanacos, skunks, and Patagonian hares. Return to the central park area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner at the boutique lodge — many lodges in the park offer a special holiday set menu on December 24th. Enjoy a festive Patagonian Christmas Eve celebration with fellow travelers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge before the northern sector excursion.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten at Laguna Azul with flamingo views — a unique Christmas Eve picnic.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) dinner at the boutique lodge — expect a multi-course set menu featuring Patagonian lamb, seafood, and local wines; approx. USD 45–60 per person for the holiday menu.

day_by_day.notes: The northern sector requires a vehicle — arrange a rental car or guided day tour from the lodge. Pumas are most active at dawn and dusk in this sector; while sightings are rare, scan open slopes with binoculars. Carry warm layers — the eastern steppe is more exposed to Patagonian wind than the sheltered western valleys.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — slow morning at the boutique lodge. Enjoy a special holiday breakfast. Take a gentle morning walk in the immediate surroundings of the lodge, breathing in the crisp Patagonian air and appreciating the extraordinary landscape you've spent the past week exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration hike — trek to Mirador Condor, a short but rewarding trail near the lodge offering elevated views of the park's central valley. Spend time reflecting on the journey: the W Trek, the glacier kayaking, the sunrise at Las Torres, and the wildlife encountered throughout the week. Pack your bags and prepare for tomorrow's departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the boutique lodge. Share stories with fellow guests, exchange contact details with trekking companions made along the way, and toast to an extraordinary Patagonian adventure with a glass of Chilean Carménère.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas morning breakfast at the lodge — expect a festive spread with fresh pastries, fruit, eggs, and sparkling wine.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge café — light meal to avoid over-eating before the farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at the boutique lodge — a celebratory multi-course meal; approx. USD 40–55 per person. Pair with a bottle of Chilean wine from the lodge's cellar.

day_by_day.notes: December 25th is a public holiday in Chile — park services, shuttles, and restaurants may operate on reduced schedules. Confirm your Day 12 transfer to Puerto Natales or the airport in advance. Check lodge checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a final morning activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake early for one last sunrise over the Paine Massif from the lodge terrace — a moment to commit to memory. Enjoy a final breakfast, complete checkout, and load luggage for the transfer to Puerto Natales.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Torres del Paine to Puerto Natales (~1.5 hrs). Arrive in Puerto Natales with time to browse the local craft markets for Patagonian souvenirs — hand-knitted wool items, calafate berry jams, and artisan leatherwork make excellent gifts. Visit the Mylodon Cave (Cueva del Milodón) Natural Monument, just 25 km from Puerto Natales, if time permits — a fascinating prehistoric cave where the remains of a giant ground sloth were discovered.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Puerto Natales before onward travel. Celebrate the completion of a truly extraordinary 12-day Patagonian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique lodge — savor it.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales — revisit a favorite spot from Day 1 or try Mesita Grande for excellent wood-fired pizza; approx. USD 12–18.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Afrigonia Restaurant in Puerto Natales — a highly regarded mid-range fusion restaurant blending Patagonian ingredients with global influences; approx. USD 25–35 per person. End with a pisco sour and calafate berry dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm onward flight or transport arrangements from Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas. If flying from Punta Arenas, allow 3+ hours for the transfer from Puerto Natales. Consider shipping any oversized souvenirs or trekking gear home from Puerto Natales post office to avoid baggage fees. Carry a copy of all park entry receipts and accommodation confirmations for border crossing if traveling onward to Argentina.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the most spectacular highlights including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. The trail winds through dramatic landscapes of granite peaks, turquoise lakes, and ancient forests, offering an unparalleled Patagonian wilderness experience.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the iconic base of the Torres del Paine towers to witness a breathtaking sunrise over the three granite monoliths reflected in the glacial lake below. This challenging 8-hour round trip hike rewards trekkers with one of the most photographed and awe-inspiring natural spectacles in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey alongside massive floating icebergs calved from the Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most impressive ice fields. This guided kayaking adventure along the lakeshore offers a unique water-level perspective of the glacier face and surrounding mountain scenery, combining water activity with raw natural beauty near the lake's edge.
experiences.location: Lago Grey Shoreline, Grey Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the stunning French Valley, a glacial amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering peaks including Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. The trail offers dramatic views of avalanches tumbling down steep cliffs and passes through native lenga beech forests alive with Andean condors soaring overhead.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Lago Pehoé Lakeside Nature Walk & Wildlife Spotting
experiences.description: Explore the serene shores of Lago Pehoé on a guided nature walk, spotting native Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and flamingos against the backdrop of the iconic Cuernos del Paine peaks. This moderate lakeside trail offers stunning reflections of the mountains on the turquoise waters and is ideal for nature photography and birdwatching.
experiences.location: Lago Pehoé Shoreline, Western Sector, Torres del Paine

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Punta Arenas airport to Torres del Paine National Park (approx. 5-hour scenic drive through Patagonian steppe). Stop at Mirador Río Serrano for first panoramic views of the park. Check in to the boutique lodge and receive a private welcome orientation with your dedicated guide.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your luxury suite, freshen up, and enjoy a sunset cocktail on the lodge terrace overlooking the iconic Torres peaks. Light introductory briefing with your guide about the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Gourmet boxed picnic prepared by the lodge, enjoyed at a scenic roadside viewpoint during the transfer
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge's fine-dining restaurant: slow-roasted Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo), local greens, and a curated Chilean Carménère from the lodge's wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all hiking gear is laid out and inspected tonight. Altitude and wind conditions can change rapidly — your guide will provide a full weather and safety briefing. Hydrate well after the long travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Early acclimatization hike around the lodge's immediate surroundings — a gentle 3 km guided walk along Lago Pehoé's northern shoreline. Spot Andean condors, guanacos, and southern lapwings. Introduction to Patagonian flora with your naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lago Pehoé Lakeside Nature Walk & Wildlife Spotting — join a fully guided 4-hour lakeside excursion with binoculars and spotting scopes provided. Observe Darwin's rheas, foxes, and flamingos in their natural habitat. Photography guidance included for capturing the turquoise lake against the Cuernos del Paine backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge for a private hot tub session overlooking the lake at sunset. Complimentary pisco sour welcome drink prepared tableside.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the lodge: freshly baked sourdough, smoked Patagonian trout, artisan cheeses, seasonal fruit, and specialty Chilean coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the lakeshore — charcuterie board, empanadas, fresh fruit, and thermos of hot soup provided by the lodge
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the lodge: king crab bisque, pan-seared centolla (Southern king crab) with herb butter, and calafate berry tart with crème fraîche

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally lighter to allow your body to adjust to Patagonian conditions and wind exposure. Sunscreen, UV-protective lip balm, and layered windproof clothing are essential even on calm days.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — depart lodge at 04:30 by private vehicle to the Las Torres trailhead. Begin the 9 km ascent by headlamp through lenga beech forest and glacial moraine. Arrive at the iconic granite towers at sunrise (approx. 06:30–07:00) for the legendary golden light reflecting on the turquoise lagoon below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend at a leisurely pace, stopping at key viewpoints. Return to lodge by early afternoon. Enjoy a restorative 60-minute deep-tissue massage at the lodge's spa upon return.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset photography session on the lodge terrace with a professional Patagonian landscape photographer. Learn composition techniques while capturing the Cuernos del Paine in evening light.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy breakfast at 04:00: overnight oats, protein bars, hard-boiled eggs, and thermos of coffee prepared by the lodge kitchen
meals.lunch: Post-hike brunch back at the lodge: eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, avocado toast, fresh-squeezed juice, and pastry basket
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the lodge — a 5-course tasting menu featuring Patagonian ingredients paired with premium Chilean wines from Casablanca Valley

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic hike in Torres del Paine. The round trip is approximately 18–20 km with 700 m elevation gain. The sunrise timing is weather-dependent — your guide will confirm departure time the evening prior based on conditions. Trekking poles and headlamps are provided.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest and recovery morning. Optional yoga session on the lodge deck with a certified instructor overlooking the lake. Alternatively, explore the lodge's curated Patagonian natural history library and map room to study the terrain ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided introduction to the W Trek route — a 3-hour reconnaissance hike along the first segment of the W from the lodge toward Mirador Cuernos. Stunning views of the Cuernos del Paine and Lago Pehoé. Return to lodge for afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing session with a local astronomer. Torres del Paine's remote location and minimal light pollution make it one of South America's premier stargazing destinations. Champagne and warm blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Lodge buffet breakfast: freshly baked croissants, local honey, granola with Patagonian berries, smoked meats, and a full egg station
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge: roasted vegetable soup, grilled sourdough with avocado and local cheese, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner for two (or group) at a private candlelit table on the terrace: grilled Patagonian beef tenderloin, truffle mashed potatoes, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a Malbec from Mendoza

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is a strategic recovery day before the multi-day W Trek segment begins. Ensure all gear is packed tonight: waterproof layers, trekking poles, gaiters, and the lodge-provided daypack. Your guide will conduct a full gear check this evening.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 Begin. Depart lodge after breakfast with private vehicle transfer to Pudeto catamaran dock. Board the private catamaran across Lago Pehoé to Refugio Paine Grande. Begin the westward hike toward Glaciar Grey (approx. 11 km, 4–5 hours). Dramatic views of the Grey Glacier tongue from multiple elevated viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mirador Glaciar Grey for extended photography and glacier observation. Watch and listen for calving events. Continue to the overnight glamping or premium refugio camp near Lago Grey. Private guide sets up camp or checks in to pre-arranged luxury refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire gathering with hot drinks and local snacks. Your guide shares the geology and glaciology of the Grey Glacier system. Clear skies may reveal the Southern Cross.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the lodge before departure: scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch on the glacier viewpoint: premium charcuterie, artisan crackers, hard cheeses, dried fruit, nuts, and hot soup from a thermos
meals.dinner: Chef-prepared hot dinner at the refugio or glamping site: hearty lentil and chorizo stew, fresh bread, and dessert brownies with dulce de leche

day_by_day.notes: This marks the beginning of the multi-day W Trek segment. Luggage transfer service is included — your main bags are transported ahead while you carry only a daypack. All premium accommodations along the route have been pre-booked exclusively.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2. Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition. Rise early for a private kayaking experience on Lago Grey. Paddle alongside massive turquoise icebergs calved from the Grey Glacier. Your certified guide provides full safety briefing, dry suits, and paddling instruction. This is an extraordinary close-up perspective of the glacier's face unavailable on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp, dry off, and begin the return hike eastward toward Refugio Paine Grande (approx. 11 km). Enjoy the reverse perspective of the glacier and mountains. Arrive at Paine Grande for check-in at the premium refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Paine Grande's elevated terrace overlooking Lago Pehoé and the Cuernos. Optional guided birdwatching session at dusk along the lakeshore.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge with dried berries, toast, peanut butter, and thermos coffee prepared at camp before kayaking
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch consumed mid-hike: wraps with smoked chicken, roasted peppers, and hummus; energy bars and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Refugio Paine Grande premium dinner: fresh pasta with Patagonian mushroom ragù, local cheese, house salad, and Chilean Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking requires moderate upper body fitness. Dry suits are provided but inform your guide of any shoulder or back concerns. Water temperature in Lago Grey is near freezing — safety protocols are strictly followed. Wind can cancel kayaking; a guided glacier viewpoint hike is the contingency.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3. Valle del Francés Trekking Day. Depart Paine Grande early and hike into the French Valley (Valle del Francés), one of Patagonia's most dramatic glacial amphitheaters. The 4-hour ascent passes through ancient lenga beech forest and opens into a cirque of hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering granite walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mirador Británico, the valley's highest viewpoint, for 360-degree panoramic views of the Cuernos del Paine, Monte Almirante Nieto, and multiple hanging glaciers. Listen for the thunder of ice avalanches. Descend at a relaxed pace, stopping at secondary viewpoints. Return to Paine Grande for the night.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory evening at the refugio. Your guide leads a guided reflection on the journey so far. Optional wine tasting session featuring three premium Chilean varietals.

meals.breakfast: Refugio hot breakfast: eggs any style, toast, jam, yogurt with granola, and fresh coffee
meals.lunch: Summit picnic at Mirador Británico: gourmet bento box with quinoa salad, smoked salmon, crackers, chocolate, and hot soup
meals.dinner: Valle del Francés celebratory dinner at Paine Grande: grilled lamb chops with chimichurri, roasted Andean potatoes, and calafate berry mousse for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is a full-day commitment — approximately 22 km round trip with 600 m elevation gain. The upper valley is exposed to Patagonian wind gusts exceeding 100 km/h; your guide will assess safety in real time. Helmets are recommended for the upper section due to occasional rockfall.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 4. Hike eastward from Paine Grande along the southern arm of the W toward Refugio Los Cuernos (approx. 11 km). The trail hugs the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld with stunning reflections of the Cuernos del Paine. Spot black-necked swans and Andean geese along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos — one of the most scenically positioned stops on the entire W Trek. Enjoy a private afternoon rest with direct views of the Cuernos del Paine towering overhead. Optional short hike to a nearby waterfall viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive sunset viewing from the refugio's premium terrace. Your guide arranges a private aperitivo hour with local wines and Patagonian nibbles as the Cuernos turn amber and rose in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Paine Grande hot breakfast: omelette with local herbs, whole grain toast, fresh fruit salad, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside trail lunch: artisan sandwich with roasted vegetables and brie, fresh apple, trail mix, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Los Cuernos premium refugio dinner: beef and root vegetable casserole, crusty bread, mixed salad, and a glass of premium Carménère

day_by_day.notes: The Lago Nordenskjöld shoreline trail offers the most consistently beautiful sustained scenery of the entire W Trek. Camera batteries should be fully charged. Wind is typically strongest in the afternoon — pace yourself accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 5 Final Segment. Depart Los Cuernos and complete the final eastern arm of the W Trek toward Las Torres base (approx. 8 km). This segment climbs through lenga beech forest and reaches the iconic moraine lake at the base of the Torres del Paine granite towers — a triumphant completion of the full W circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Celebratory moment at the Torres base lagoon — your guide leads a private toast with sparkling wine at the summit viewpoint. Descend to the Las Torres trailhead and board a private vehicle back to the boutique lodge. Return to your luxury suite for a long-awaited hot shower and full luggage reunion.
day_by_day.evening: W Trek completion celebration dinner at the lodge. The chef prepares a special multi-course feast in honor of your achievement. Complimentary bottle of premium Champagne presented by lodge management.

meals.breakfast: Los Cuernos hot breakfast: French toast with berry compote, scrambled eggs, and fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Summit celebration picnic at the Torres base: smoked salmon blinis, aged cheeses, grapes, dark chocolate, and sparkling cider
meals.dinner: W Trek completion gala dinner at the lodge: five-course tasting menu — amuse-bouche, centolla ceviche, wild mushroom risotto, Patagonian lamb rack, and a showstopping calafate berry soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 completes the legendary W Trek — approximately 80 km total over 5 days. Your guide will present each guest with a handwritten completion certificate from the lodge. This evening is intentionally celebratory and unhurried — no early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury rest and recovery morning. Enjoy the lodge's full spa menu: 90-minute hot stone massage, infrared sauna session, and a revitalizing facial using Patagonian botanical extracts. Sleep in and take breakfast at your leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe with a local baqueano (gaucho). Explore areas of the park accessible only on horseback. Spot guanacos, rheas, and condors from the saddle. Duration: 3 hours. All riding levels welcome.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special celebration at the lodge. The chef prepares a traditional Chilean Nochebuena feast. Live folk music by a local Patagonian musician. The lodge team decorates the dining room for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely lodge brunch: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, seasonal fruit platter, fresh juices, and specialty coffee — served until 11:00
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch: chilled gazpacho, quinoa and roasted vegetable bowl, sparkling water, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Nochebuena feast: traditional pan de pascua (Chilean Christmas bread), roasted Patagonian lamb with herb crust, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent chocolate and calafate berry yule log

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve at Torres del Paine is a magical experience — the long Patagonian summer light means it doesn't get fully dark until after 22:00. The lodge team creates a warm festive atmosphere. Guests are invited to join a communal toast at midnight if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — private guided half-day nature photography expedition to Laguna Azul in the lesser-visited northeastern sector of the park. This remote lagoon offers spectacular reflections of Monte Almirante Nieto and is a prime flamingo habitat. Access is by private 4WD vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for a Christmas Day asado (traditional Argentine/Chilean barbecue) prepared by the lodge's head chef on the outdoor terrace. Guests gather around the open fire for a relaxed, festive afternoon of dining, wine, and conversation.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell stargazing session and private whisky tasting curated by the lodge sommelier — featuring three premium Scotch single malts paired with dark Patagonian chocolate. Reflect on the journey's highlights with your guide over a final nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning breakfast in bed: croissants, smoked trout, scrambled eggs, fresh orange juice, and a Champagne mimosa delivered to your suite
meals.lunch: Christmas asado on the terrace: whole-roasted Patagonian lamb, grilled chorizo, chimichurri, roasted peppers, fresh salads, and premium Malbec
meals.dinner: Light Christmas evening dinner: leftover asado tapas, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, and a selection of Chilean dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is uniquely memorable — the remote wilderness setting combined with the lodge's warm hospitality creates an unforgettable festive experience. Laguna Azul is often visited by flamingos in December; binoculars are essential. Confirm 4WD vehicle booking the evening prior.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the lodge grounds — a slow, reflective 1-hour stroll with your guide along the Lago Pehoé shoreline. Say farewell to the Torres del Paine landscape as the first light illuminates the granite towers one last time. Return for a final full lodge breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the lodge and depart on private luxury transfer back to Punta Arenas (approx. 5-hour drive). Scenic stops at Mirador Río Serrano and a traditional estancia for a farewell mate (herbal tea) with local gauchos.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Punta Arenas for onward flights or overnight stay. If time permits before departure, visit the historic Cementerio Municipal Sara Braun — a remarkable UNESCO-listed site — and enjoy a final dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the lodge: full spread of all lodge favorites — smoked trout, eggs, pastries, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional estancia lunch during transfer stop: homemade empanadas, fresh bread, local cheese, and mate
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Punta Arenas at Restaurante Santolla: king crab in multiple preparations, local wines, and a classic Patagonian dessert of dulce de leche with meringue

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all departure logistics are confirmed the evening prior: flight times, transfer duration, and any last-minute luggage arrangements. The lodge concierge will assist with packing any purchased regional products (wines, preserves, wool goods) for safe transport. Allow extra time at Punta Arenas airport for potential wind-related delays.
